summary: Implemented the bounded HTTP/TCP health probe with injectable clock and fetch, default 2s/5s/90s timings, structured attempt/elapsed results, abort-bounded attempts, body-safe diagnostics, and 14 focused tests; typecheck, lint, focused tests, full suite, and build pass.

payload.agentOutputExcerpt: Implemented the bounded HTTP/TCP health probe with injectable clock and fetch, default 2s/5s/90s timings, structured attempt/elapsed results, abort-bounded attempts, body-safe diagnostics, and 14 focused tests; typecheck, lint, focused tests, full suite, and build pass.
decisions: HTTP probes use redirect:'manual' so a 3xx is healthy without following the redirect.
Per-attempt timeout uses a clock timer plus AbortController and races the operation, so even an abort-ignoring client cannot exceed the attempt bound.
An unhealthy probe returns a ProbeResult instead of throwing; lifecycle maps it to HealthError exit 4.
Invalid probe options throw UsageError exit 1 with stable code INVALID_PROBE_OPTIONS.
Probe defaults are sourced from APP_SPEC_DEFAULTS to avoid drift with config schema defaults.
interfaces: ProbeResult {state, healthy, kind, port, target, attempts, elapsedMs, lastStatus, lastError, intervalMs, timeoutMs, startupMs}
ProbeFailure {kind, code, message, status, timeoutMs, causeCode}
ProbeClock {now, sleep, setTimeout, clearTimeout}, ProbeFetch, TcpConnector
warnings: New stable code INVALID_PROBE_OPTIONS (exit 1) for invalid probe inputs.
ADD-1.4 must treat an unhealthy ProbeResult as the health failure that triggers container cleanup and exit 4.
No probe consumer exists yet, so there were no consumer tests beyond this module's suite.
validationLimitations: Gated host integration was not run; tests/integration/add.test.ts does not exist yet and this task requires no real host.
payload.taskDescription: Implement probe.ts with an injectable clock and fetch. HTTP mode issues GET http://127.0.0.1:<port><health_path>, treats 2xx and 3xx as healthy, and any other status, network error, or timeout as an attempt failure. TCP mode connects to 127.0.0.1:<port>. Repeat at the declared interval until healthy or the startup budget expires, and return a structured result with attempts, last error, and elapsed time. Tests use a local HTTP server and fake clock to cover immediate success, success after retries, 500 responses, connection refused, timeout, TCP success, and budget exhaustion.
